recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No FHIR core follow-up is needed unless the work group separately changes how ElementDefinition.base is populated or consumed by code generators.
issue_request: FHIR-8310 was a Published/Persuasive with Modification FHIR-core StructureDefinition issue about profiles that constrain max to 1 and thereby lose information that the base element was repeating. The approved resolution was to add basePath, baseMin, and baseMax to ElementDefinition.
initial_application: The Jira comment records svn revision 5924. No current git commit explicitly names FHIR-8310, but the same application history shows ddb1f8c4e0916fada828b645a84c2c90f59329e2 (#6066, svn r5923) adding ElementDefinition.base and 74950f48e21290a8d95baa474e74c2d2d3034e11 (#6066, svn r5924) adding base invariants.
additional_context: FHIR-6066, FHIR-6093, and FHIR-6340 share the same ElementDefinition.base resolution. FHIR-6093 and FHIR-6340 are already represented on the combined branch, while FHIR-6066 is the seed audited here. Direct FHIR-8310 community searches found no conflicting Zulip or Confluence evidence.
reconciliation: No source change was made because current ElementDefinition source defines base.path, base.min, and base.max as required when base is present; base.max explicitly preserves the base maximum cardinality and notes its role in JSON serialization and code generation.
